newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui Eng unit wins Y35 bln oil facility orders.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui Eng unit wins Y35 bln oil facility orders.

text.p: Modec Inc, a subsidiary of Mitsui Engineering & Shipbuilding Co Ltd, said on Wednesday it had won three contracts, worth roughly 35 billion yen, to build floating oil production and storage facilities.

The three firms that placed orders are Australia's BHP Petroleum Pty Ltd, a subsidiary of Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, Mexico's state-owned Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex), and Marathon Petroleum Gabon LDC, an affiliate of Marathon Oil Co of the United States.
Modec won a contract to build a one-million barrel floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) facility for BHP Petroleum, a Modec spokesman said.
The FPSO, to be built by modifying an old oil tanker at the Jurong shipyard in Singapore by next spring, will be used in offshore oilfields in the Timor Sea.

The Japanese marine engineering firm, along with trading house Mitsui & Co Ltd, also received an order from Pemex to build a floating storage and offloading (FSO) facility with storage capacity of 2.2 million barrels.
Modec will build the FSO, to be operated at the Cantarell block off the Yucatan Peninsula, by remodeling a used ultra large crude carrier (ULCC) at the Jurong shipyard, the spokesman said.
The other order, which Modec won with trading house Nissho Iwai Corp, is for a one-million barrel FSO and a mobile offshore production unit (MOPU) for Marathon Petroleum Gabon.
The two units will be sent to Gabon, west Africa, by the end of the year, he added.
